question: Under what conditional claim is a beginning said to take place when desire is present and the matter is stated thus?
premises: A desire forms a stated condition.
The statement is marked by a connective and quotative form.
A beginning is posited in relation to that condition.
inference: If desire is present, the beginning of the procedure is said to follow as stated.
uncertainties: The object of desire is not specified in this verse.
It is unclear whether prakramaḥ is the beginning of a mantra or of a rite.
plain_english: If there is desire, then thus the beginning is said to take place.
